statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most clones, 92.4%, expanded at a stable exponential rate, with yearly growth ranging from 5% for DNMT3A and TP53 up to over 50% for SRSF2.
statements.evidence: We find that 92.4% of clones expanded at a stable exponential rate over the study period, with different mutations driving substantially different growth rates, ranging from 5% (DNMT3A and TP53) to more than 50% per year

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In this cohort, clones grew faster in men than in women.
statements.evidence: Growth rates of clones with the same mutation differed by approximately ±5% per year, proportionately affecting slow drivers more substantially.
statements.note: The abstract describes within-mutation variability in growth rates but makes no comparison between sexes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clones carrying mutations that drove faster growth had a higher risk of malignant progression.
statements.evidence: mutations driving faster clonal growth carry a higher risk of malignant progression
statements.note: The abstract links faster-growing clones to a greater risk of becoming malignant.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: DNMT3A-mutant clones expanded mainly early in life and showed slower growth in old age.
statements.evidence: DNMT3A-mutant clones preferentially expanded early in life and displayed slower growth in old age

statements.text: New loci implicated DNA damage repair genes, CD164 in stem-cell homing, and SETBP1 in myeloid oncogenesis.

statements.label: supported

statements.text: SSK1, activated by β-gal, eliminated both mouse and human senescent cells regardless of inducer or cell type.

statements.note: The abstract states SSK1 clears mouse and human senescent cells independent of inducer and type.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In aged mice the compound cleared senescent cells across tissues, lowered inflammation, and restored physical function.

statements.label: supported
